purpose: Independent practice of C1.3 — naming multi-step pattern rules and using them to extend patterns several terms ahead.
student_learning_goal: I can name a multi-step pattern rule and use it to build the next term.

parts.student_instructions: Look at each pattern. Decide whether the rule is SINGLE-STEP or MULTI-STEP. Then write the rule on the line.

Strip C: 6-cell number row 2, 6, 4, 12, 10, 30 (rule ×3 then -2, compound). Beside each, two writing lines: 'Single-step or multi-step? ___. Rule: ___.'

parts.answer_key: Cells 4-6: 12, 11, 15. (Pattern: 5, 9, 8, 12, 11, 15. Each cycle of 2 has net effect +3.) Term 10: pattern continues 14, 18, 17, 21. So term 10 = 21. (Computation: term 1 = 5; +3 net effect per 2-term cycle; from term 1 to term 10 is 9 jumps which is 4 full cycles plus one extra +4 — start + 4×3 + 4 = 5 + 12 + 4 = 21. Accept variations.)

parts.part_title: Part 3: Invent your own multi-step rule
parts.student_instructions: Pick your own starting number AND a 2-step compound rule. Write both on the lines, then fill in 6 terms. Then predict term 8.

parts.answer_key: Any valid 2-step compound rule with a starting number. Examples: Start 1, rule +5 then -2 → 1, 6, 4, 9, 7, 12, term 8 = 17. Start 10, rule ×2 then +1 → 10, 21, 43, 87, 175, 351 (gets large fast), term 8 = ... use calculator. Correct if the rule is applied consistently across all 6 visible terms AND the term 8 prediction follows the rule.

early_finisher_prompt: If you finish, try a 3-STEP compound rule (e.g., +5, then +3, then -2). Build at least 6 terms and predict term 9.
teacher_notes: Lesson 2 consolidation. The most diagnostic part is Part 2 — children who fill cells 4-6 correctly AND predict term 10 by reasoning about the cycle (rather than computing every term) are at L3+ on C1.3. Children who get cells 4-6 right but skip term 10 may need the cycle-net-effect scaffold. Part 3 is open-ended — accept any valid compound rule applied consistently. Children who invent multi-step rules with multiplication (e.g., ×2 then +1) are showing L4 thinking and should be flagged for Grade 4 enrichment.
